comments.text: I’m a pharmacy technician working in the ED, responsible for complete medication reviews with patients. We check their online prescription history but also interview them for last doses (to understand compliance), over the counter medications and supplements and any relevant pharmaceutical information. We can flag issues for the pharmacists and doctors who don’t have 30-60 minutes to do full med histories. Especially important for seniors or people in care facilities, who often have a ton of drugs. We also find patients are more likely to be honest with us because we’re not poking or prodding them, we’re just talking. Amazing how often people just need someone to listen and we find out lots of additional important information that they think is “probably nothing”.

I was working, for a hospital, and while my coworker was carrying an 80lbs condenser fan motor up a ships ladder to the roof, it fell... 20 feet... and the right side of my face was the landing spot... I went home that night, ate dinner, went to bed, and decided in the morning to go to the ER when I realized I couldn't feel myself brushing my teeth... Found that I had 3 broken bones, a severed nerve that leads from my sinus to my teeth? and a severe concussion that could have become life threatening if undiscovered/treated (according to the doctors). But according to about 5 different doctors and an ungodly amount of nurses, I was very, VERY lucky to actually be alive, let alone in such stable condition.
